**PRELIMINARY FEDERAL TITLE VII MEMORANDUM**
**To:** Product Counsel / HR
**Re:** Rivera Charge — Threshold Plausibility Assessment
**Date of Analysis:** 2025-03-01
**Scope:** US Federal Title VII Only

---

### I. Covered-Employer Status

**Conclusion: Northwind is a covered employer.**

Title VII defines a covered employer as one affecting commerce with 15 or more employees "for each working day in each of 20 or more calendar weeks" in the current or preceding year. 42 U.S.C. § 2000e(b) [SRC-STATUTE-2000E]. In *Walters v. Metropolitan Educational Enterprises*, 519 U.S. 202, 207–212 (1997) [SRC-SCOTUS-WALTERS-1997], the Supreme Court held that the "payroll method" counts employment relationships, not whether the employee actually worked or received compensation on a given day.

Northwind maintained employment relationships with 16 individuals throughout each relevant workweek [F-PAYROLL-16]. The two part-time employees who did not work Fridays nonetheless remained in an active employment relationship on those days [F-PARTTIME-FRIDAY]. Under *Walters*, they count. This pattern persisted for 22 calendar weeks in both the current and preceding years [F-WEEKS-22], exceeding the 20-week jurisdictional threshold. **16 ≥ 15; 22 ≥ 20. Northwind is covered.**

---

### II. Rivera's Transfer-Discrimination Claim

**Conclusion: Plausible claim; not a determination of ultimate liability.**

Under *Muldrow v. City of St. Louis*, No. 22-193 (Apr. 17, 2024) [SRC-SCOTUS-MULDROW-2024], a transfer-discrimination plaintiff must show "some injury respecting employment terms or conditions." The Court expressly vacated the Eighth Circuit's "materially significant disadvantage" test and clarified that equal pay does not defeat the claim.

Rivera's injuries are concrete: loss of a Monday–Friday hybrid schedule in favor of rotating nights and weekends, loss of supervisory client work, and loss of a take-home vehicle [F-RIVERA-TRANSFER]. A less experienced male replaced her in the client-lead role [F-MALE-REPLACEMENT]. A preserved manager message states the client-facing lead "should be a man" [F-MOTIVE-SEX]. These facts, taken together, satisfy the *Muldrow* "some harm" threshold and support a plausible inference of sex-based discrimination under § 2000e-2(a)(1) [SRC-STATUTE-2000E-2].

**Caveats:** Authentication and admissibility of the manager message have not been litigated. Credibility, employer defenses (e.g., legitimate business reason), and discovery outcomes are unassessed. This is threshold plausibility, not a liability finding.

---

### III. Rivera's Retaliation Claim

**Conclusion: Plausible claim; material adversity required and plausibly met.**

Title VII prohibits retaliation against an employee who opposes a practice made unlawful by the statute. 42 U.S.C. § 2000e-3(a) [SRC-STATUTE-2000E-3]. Rivera's April 22, 2024 complaint to HR — that her manager reserved client-lead assignments for men and that she reasonably believed this was sex discrimination [F-RIVERA-PROTECTED-COMPLAINT] — is classic protected opposition activity.

The transfer was finalized on May 1, 2024, only nine days after the complaint [F-NOTICE-DATE]. Under *Burlington Northern & Santa Fe Railway Co. v. White*, 548 U.S. 53, 61–73 (2006) [SRC-SCOTUS-BURLINGTON-2006], retaliation requires "material adversity" — conduct that might dissuade a reasonable worker from making or supporting a discrimination charge. The loss of supervisory work, take-home vehicle, and stable daytime schedule is plausibly material. A preserved HR note attributes the transfer to "reducing friction" after the complaint [F-MOTIVE-COMPLAINT], supporting an inference of retaliatory motive if authenticated.

*Muldrow* did not alter the retaliation standard; it expressly left *Burlington*'s material-adversity test intact for retaliation claims.

---

### IV. Timeliness of Rivera's Charge

**Conclusion: Timely under the 300-day FEPA window.**

The ordinary charge-filing deadline is 180 days. 42 U.S.C. § 2000e-5(e)(1) [SRC-STATUTE-2000E-5]. However, when the complainant initially institutes proceedings with an authorized state or local fair-employment-practices agency, the deadline extends to 300 days (or 30 days after notice the state agency terminated proceedings, whichever is earlier) [SRC-STATUTE-2000E-5; SRC-EEOC-FILING-CHARGE].

Rivera jointly filed with EEOC and the authorized state FEPA on February 20, 2025 — 295 days after final notice on May 1, 2024 [F-FILING-295, F-NOTICE-DATE]. The state agency enforces a law prohibiting sex discrimination and is authorized to grant or seek relief [F-FEPA]. Rivera received no notice of state-agency termination before filing [F-NO-FEPA-TERMINATION]. **295 < 300. The charge is timely.**

---

### V. Lee's Retaliation Claim

**Conclusion: No Title VII protected activity on supplied facts.**

Title VII's anti-retaliation provision protects only those who (1) oppose a practice made unlawful by Title VII or (2) participate in a Title VII proceeding. 42 U.S.C. § 2000e-3(a) [SRC-STATUTE-2000E-3]. Lee complained only that a loading dock was physically unsafe [F-LEE-SAFETY-ONLY]. Lee never opposed a practice believed to violate Title VII and did not participate in any Title VII process. A physical-safety complaint, without connection to an enumerated protected characteristic, is not protected activity under federal Title VII. Lee's otherwise identical transfer therefore cannot sustain a Title VII retaliation claim on this record.

---

### VI. Adversarial-Note Trap Dispositions

| Trap | Disposition | Rationale |
|------|-------------|-----------|
| T-STALE-CA8 | **Rejected** | *Muldrow* (2024) vacated the 8th Circuit judgment; the significance test is no longer controlling for discrimination harm. |
| T-STANDARDS-CONFLATED | **Rejected** | *Muldrow* requires some harm for discrimination (not zero harm) and left *Burlington*'s material-adversity standard intact for retaliation. |
| T-WORKED-DAYS | **Rejected** | *Walters* holds employment relationships — not actual work or pay — determine the headcount. |
| T-180-DAYS | **Rejected** | The 300-day window applies in deferral jurisdictions with an authorized FEPA; Rivera's 295-day filing is timely. |
| T-SAFETY-PROTECTED | **Rejected** | Title VII protects opposition to enumerated-characteristic discrimination, not generic safety complaints. |

---

### VII. Advisory Posture

This memorandum assesses **threshold plausibility, not ultimate liability**. The evidence-admissibility questions (manager message, HR note), credibility determinations, and discovery have not been evaluated. State-law and non-Title VII federal claims (e.g., OSHA) are outside scope. Remedies have not been quantified.

**Recommended next step:** Prompt qualified employment counsel and/or EEOC review for full case assessment.
